findings.evidence: evaluate() explicitly drops the still-forming 5-minute context candle before computing ATR/EMA: `five = [b for b in aggregate_five_minutes(today) if b.start + timedelta(minutes=5) <= current.start]` (strategy.py:88-92). protective_exit() computes `five = aggregate_five_minutes(validate_bars(bars, now))` with no equivalent exclusion (strategy.py:179), then uses `five[-1].close` for the trend_failed comparison and `b.high for b in eligible` (eligible drawn from the same possibly-incomplete `five`) for the trailing-stop high (strategy.py:183-189). Trigger: any cycle where 'now' falls inside a partially-completed 5-minute bucket while a position is open (i.e. most cycles, since positions are marked every runtime cycle at 10s granularity per config.py cycle_seconds). Consequence: the trailing stop and 'trend_failed' exit can be computed from an incomplete final 5-minute bar rather than the last fully-closed one, contradicting the module's own docstring ('Only completed, contiguous intraday bars enter rules') and this function's own docstring ('optional completed-bar exit'). This function is shared verbatim by live runtime.py:222-228, replay.py:825-827 (the qualification backtest), and shadow.py:182-187 (the shadow-qualification simulator), so the bias is self-consistent across all three but is not what the code claims to do, and could cause spurious premature exits (or delayed tightening) versus the documented completed-bar model. Confidence is high on the structural asymmetry from the given source; confidence on functional severity is moderate because aggregate_five_minutes' exact truncation behavior is defined in quantpilot/paper/strategy.py, which was not included in this review packet.
findings.proposal: Apply the same exclusion evaluate() uses (drop any 5-minute bucket whose end exceeds the current minute) before computing atr/ema/high inside protective_exit, so trailing-stop and trend_failed decisions only ever consult fully-closed 5-minute bars; add a regression test asserting protective_exit's output is unchanged when extra partial-bucket 1m bars are appended mid-bucket.

findings.evidence: replay.py hardcodes FEE_BPS=1.40527, SELL_TAX_BPS=20.0, ENTRY_CUTOFF_MINUTES=30, LIQUIDATION_MINUTES=20 as module constants (replay.py:37-40), and shadow.py hardcodes the same round-trip cost as the literal `31.40527`/`11.40527` in four places (shadow.py:147,227,338,363) rather than reading them from Policy. store.configure() only forbids changing 'version' and 'initial_capital' (store.py:129-130); fee_bps, sell_tax_bps, slippage_bps, entry_cutoff_minutes and liquidation_minutes can be changed at any time, including while strategy_generation is already 'intraday_v2' and control is 'running', by bumping the policy version. admitted() (deployment.py:53-74) binds admission to IMPLEMENTATION_HASH (a hash of the source code, i.e. Field defaults) and to the frozen candidate/report hashes, but never compares the live store.policy.fee_bps/sell_tax_bps/slippage_bps/entry_cutoff_minutes/liquidation_minutes against the values the admitted evidence was actually computed with. Trigger: operator calls store.configure({'fee_bps': X, ...}) after a strategy is already paper_eligible/admitted. Consequence: risk.py's live entry_size/loss_budget (which read policy.fee_bps etc. live, e.g. risk.py:104-129,170) and authorize_order's entry-cutoff check (risk.py:206) immediately start using the new values, while admitted() keeps returning True because none of its checks reference these fields — the strategy keeps 'paper_eligible' status even though its live cost/timing behavior no longer matches the backtested/shadow-validated assumptions baked into replay.py/shadow.py.
findings.proposal: Include the admission-time values of fee_bps/sell_tax_bps/slippage_bps/entry_cutoff_minutes/liquidation_minutes in the frozen candidate or report (or hash them alongside candidate_hash), and have admitted() reject when the currently configured policy's values diverge from what was validated.

findings.evidence: The approved plan requires '지연·미체결·갭·부분체결 민감도 별도 보고' (docs/plans/intraday-redesign-20260911.md:16). run_study() computes three sensitivity scenarios — delay_2m, half_fills, no_fills (evaluation.py:249-262) — and stores them under result['sensitivity'] inside the 'holdout' evidence record. evaluate_candidate()'s report construction (evaluation.py:412-432) has no 'sensitivity' key at all and never reads result['sensitivity'] anywhere in the function body (evaluation.py:316-437), so this data is computed but never surfaces in the qualification report that admit()/admitted() and any downstream reviewer would consult. findings.proposal: Add the missing sensitivity dict (or a summary of it) to the report returned by evaluate_candidate, and add a gap-sensitivity replay scenario (e.g. simulate a session with a synthetic overnight/intraday price gap at the open of the eligible window) alongside delay_2m/half_fills/no_fills.

Any deployment whose store.policy.initial_capital differs from the hardcoded 5,000,000 would make admit() always fail with the wrong error, i.e. the exact admission workflow F2 was supposed to fix becomes unusable. The paired regression test also does not discriminate pre-fix vs post-fix behavior (the added 4-bar "partial" group is already excluded by aggregate_five_minutes' own group-size==5 check, independent of the new filter), so F1's fix, while harmless, is not actually demonstrated to change any behavior. Also, F2's original finding cited shadow.py's hardcoded round-trip-cost literals (31.40527/11.40527) alongside replay.py's; this diff does not touch shadow.py at all, so that half of F2's original evidence remains unaddressed. findings.location: quantpilot/paper/intraday/deployment.py admit() (changes comprehension over VALIDATED_POLICY) vs quantpilot/paper/store.py:124-130 (configure's unconditional immutable_policy_field guard)
findings.evidence: VALIDATED_POLICY includes `"initial_capital": 5_000_000`. admit()'s `changes = {key: value for key, value in VALIDATED_POLICY.items() if getattr(store.policy, key) != value}` will include "initial_capital" whenever the live store's initial_capital differs from 5,000,000, and the subsequent `store.configure(changes, store.policy.version)` call will raise `ValueError("immutable_policy_field")` from store.py:129-130, which fires for ANY value of initial_capital present in changes, not just an actual attempted-change conflict. This breaks admit() for any account whose funding level differs from the hardcoded validated figure — precisely the workflow this correction round targets for F2 — and is not exercised by any new or shown test; the new test (test_admission_is_bound_to_validated_runtime_policy) manually excludes "initial_capital" before its own direct configure() call, evidencing the author's awareness of this exact hazard without applying the fix inside admit() itself.
findings.proposal: Exclude "initial_capital" (and "version") from the VALIDATED_POLICY-derived diff in admit(), mirroring the exclusion already applied in the new test, and add a regression test that calls admit() (not just store.configure()+manual admission-record injection) against a store whose initial_capital differs from VALIDATED_POLICY's value to lock in correct behavior.

findings.evidence: validate_bars(bars, now) rejects any bar where `bar.start + timedelta(minutes=1) > now` (strategy.py:139-140) before aggregate_five_minutes ever groups them; aggregate_five_minutes only emits a bucket when all 5 consecutive 1-minute bars are present (strategy.py:177: `if len(group) != 5 ...: continue`). Therefore every bucket returned by `aggregate_five_minutes(validate_bars(bars, now))` already has its last (5th) bar's start+1min <= now, i.e. bucket.start+5min <= now always holds — the newly added filter `if b.start + timedelta(minutes=5) <= now` in protective_exit can never actually exclude anything given these preconditions, making it a provable no-op relative to the prior code. The paired regression test adds only 4 extra 1-minute bars (100-103) forming an incomplete 5-bar bucket, which aggregate_five_minutes' own `len(group) != 5` check already excludes independent of the new guard — so this test would pass identically against the pre-fix code and does not demonstrate the guard changes any observable behavior.
findings.proposal: Either accept this as intentional defensive/documentation-parity code (harmless, matches evaluate()'s style) and note it as non-functional, or construct a regression test that actually exercises a case distinguishing pre-fix from post-fix behavior, to make the guard's necessity verifiable rather than tautological.

F2-admit-initial-capital-immutable-conflict: admit()이 store.configure() 호출 전에 `store.policy.initial_capital`, `store.get("initial_capital")`, `store.get("cash")`가 모두 VALIDATED_POLICY의 5,000,000과 일치하는지 먼저 검사하고, 불일치 시 어떤 쓰기도 일어나기 전에 `ValueError("validated_initial_capital_required")`로 즉시 중단한다. changes 딕셔너리에서도 "initial_capital"을 명시적으로 제외해 store.py의 immutable_policy_field 가드와 충돌할 여지를 근본적으로 없앴다. 새 파라미터화 테스트가 3,000,000 케이스에서 admit()을 직접 호출해 예외·미변경 정책 버전·미변경 cash(3M 그대로)·빈 admission 레코드를 모두 검증하고, 5,000,000 케이스에서는 정상 승인과 정책 반영(slippage_bps=10, max_positions=2)을 검증한다 — proposal이 요구한 "admit()을 직접 호출하는 회귀 테스트"에 정확히 부합한다.

F2-shadow-hardcoded-costs-unaddressed: shadow.py가 VALIDATED_POLICY를 import해 ENTRY_COST_RATE/EXIT_COST_RATE를 계산하고, 기존에 산재하던 31.40527/11.40527 및 0.95/0.99/0.25/0.005/0.01/30분/20분/15초/5,000,000 등 모든 매직넘버를 VALIDATED_POLICY 참조로 치환했다. 각 치환값을 원래 하드코딩 값과 대조한 결과 수치 차이는 없음(순수 리팩터). replay.py·strategy.py도 동일한 단일 출처를 공유하도록 이미 바뀌어 있고, 기존 IMPLEMENTATION_HASH가 `intraday/*.py` 전체를 해싱하므로 향후 값이 벌어지면 해시가 깨진다 — "silently diverge" 우려의 근본 원인이 제거되었다.

부수적으로 replay.py의 CAPITAL이 `5_000_000.0`(float)에서 `VALIDATED_POLICY["initial_capital"]`(int)로 타입만 바뀌었는데, 이후 전부 나눗셈/곱셈 컨텍스트에서만 쓰여 Python이 자동으로 float로 승격하므로 기능적 영향은 없다고 판단했다. 이 세션은 StructuredOutput 외 도구가 제공되지 않아 정적 diff/테스트 코드 대조만으로 판정했으며, "37 cases / full offline suite" 실행 결과는 직접 재현하지 않았다(과제 지시상 도구·외부 호출 금지).
unresolvedRisks: replay.py의 CAPITAL이 float 리터럴(5_000_000.0)에서 VALIDATED_POLICY의 int(5_000_000)로 타입이 바뀌었다 — 현재 사용처는 모두 나눗셈/곱셈뿐이라 실질 영향은 없어 보이지만, 향후 정수 전용 연산(예: 나머지 연산, 직렬화 스키마 비교)이 추가되면 잠재적 타입 불일치가 될 수 있다.
admit()의 신규 자본 가드는 store.transaction()의 롤백 시맨틱에 의존하지 않는다(예외가 어떤 쓰기보다도 먼저 발생하므로) — 다만 store.transaction()의 실제 커밋/롤백 동작 자체는 이번 diff에 포함되지 않아 이 리뷰에서 직접 검증하지 못했다.
이 리뷰는 정적 소스 대조로만 수행되었고 scripts/verify-paper.py 등 실제 pytest 실행은 이 세션에서 수행하지 않았다 — 과제 설명에 언급된 '37 cases 통과' 및 'full offline suite 진행 중'은 독립적으로 재확인되지 않았다.
cash가 정확히 initial_capital과 같아야 한다는 3중 검사는 '승인은 거래 시작 전 상태에서만 발생한다(control=stopped, orders/positions 없음)'는 기존 불변식에 의존한다 — 이 전제가 깨지는 향후 변경(예: cash를 조작할 수 있는 관리 경로)이 생기면 정당한 후속 승인이 부당하게 거부될 수 있다.
